name: BrowserCloud

modes.label: Hobby plan browser-hours (120 h for $19)
modes.note: Effective rate = plan fee / included browser-hours ($19 / 120 h). Credits also pay bandwidth, proxies and agents from the same pool. Overage beyond the included hours is not published: usage above 120 h is priced at this same rate as an approximation.

modes.label: Startup plan browser-hours (1000 h for $99)
modes.note: Effective rate = plan fee / included browser-hours ($99 / 1000 h). Credits also pay bandwidth, proxies and agents from the same pool. Overage beyond the included hours is not published: usage above 1000 h is priced at this same rate as an approximation.

modes.label: Business plan browser-hours (3000 h for $249)
modes.note: Effective rate = plan fee / included browser-hours ($249 / 3000 h). Credits also pay bandwidth, proxies and agents from the same pool. Overage beyond the included hours is not published: usage above 3000 h is priced at this same rate as an approximation.

modes.label: Unlimited plan: dedicated cluster, flat monthly per parallel sessions
modes.note: Dedicated cluster with no credit caps. Flat $/month for N parallel sessions, unlimited credits (browser hours, HTTP API and proxy traffic presumably included; not itemised). Purchase is via 'Contact Sales' / 'Get started' buttons, but prices are published. >400 sessions custom. Per-browser vCPU/RAM unpublished.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: $19/month = 120 browser-hours (credits pool); fee treated as usage credit at the effective hourly rate. Annual billing up to 20% off (no annual table). Changing plans resets the cycle and charges the full new fee (no proration). Unused credits expire each period.

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: $99/month = 1000 browser-hours (credits pool); fee treated as usage credit at the effective hourly rate.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: $249/month = 3000 browser-hours (credits pool); fee treated as usage credit at the effective hourly rate.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Unlimited (dedicated cluster)
plans.note: Fee is the pool tier price (see mode unlimited-dedicated-cluster): 100/200/300/400 sessions = $690/$940/$1,100/$1,250 per month. Includes Advanced Stealth, residential proxies, custom IP pools, SLA.

free.trial: 14-day free trial on all paid plans, no credit card required. The Free plan (1,000 credits/month = 1 browser-hour, 1 concurrent, 15-min sessions) can be used indefinitely.

features.ip_note: Datacenter (12 credits/MB) and residential (80 credits/MB) proxies with rotation on all plans; residential ~$12.67/GB on Hobby ($19 = 1.5 GB), ~$7.92/GB on Startup. Auto CAPTCHA solving from Hobby ($19) up (not Free); proxy geotargeting Hobby and up; Advanced Stealth, premium residential proxies and bring-your-own-proxy Startup ($99) and up; custom IP pools Enterprise/Unlimited only.

caveats: Browser-hour, bandwidth, residential-proxy and browser-agent charges all draw from one monthly credit pool. Displayed hours/GB are alternative uses of credits, not additive included pools. Dedicated-cluster/unlimited plans are a different regime.
Overage and eight-hour session eligibility need detailed plan confirmation; cannot stack the hours and traffic equivalents.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.
Browser-hour examples are explicitly not 4-vCPU/8-GiB general-compute equivalents. Browser CPU/RAM allocation is unspecified.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

2026-09-28 pricing page: Free 1 h / 1 concurrent / 15-min sessions; Hobby $19 120 h / 5; Startup $99 1,000 h / 50; Business $249 3,000 h / 100; Enterprise custom. No overage price and no browser CPU/RAM published. Hourly prices are plan fee / included hours; usage above the plan's hours is priced at the same rate (unverified: you may need a bigger plan).
Credits do not roll over: 'Unused API credits are not transferred to the next subscription period.' Fee-as-credit therefore acts as a hard monthly minimum per plan.

Overage is ON by default on paid plans ("overage fees are charged per credit at the specified overage rate"), but the per-credit overage rate is not published. Free hard-stops at its limit. No 8-hour session limit on official pages: paid plans are marketed as unlimited session time, Free is capped at 15 min, default session timeout 30 s (timeout param). Supersedes the "Overage and eight-hour session eligibility" caveat.

CONFLICT between official pages: the pricing page says '1 hour of browser time 1,000 credits' and '1 MB Residential 80 credits', but docs/other/credits-cost says browser instance '1 credit / second' (= 3,600 credits/h) and 'Residential 110 credits / MB'. If the docs were right, Hobby's 120,000 credits would buy about 33 h, not 120 h (rates 3.6x the card's). The card follows the pricing page (newer, (c)2026 bundle; docs footer (c)2025).

fleet.tiers: Free 1; Hobby 5; Startup 50; Business 100; Enterprise custom 300+; dedicated-cluster offer advertises 100–400+ parallel sessions.
fleet.notes: Concurrent managed browsers. 10/50 fit Startup; 300/1,000 need custom/dedicated arrangement rather than inferred unlimited capacity. Verification and provisioning timing not stated.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

harness_api.note: The product is a remote Chrome reached over CDP/WebSocket plus HTTP APIs (/content, /pdf, /screenshot, /scenario). AI integrations (Browser Use, n8n, Zapier, Make) run the agent on the customer's side and point it at the CDP URL. No in-sandbox agent harness or API to drive one. The pricing page's 'Browser Agent' label is only a credit category.

guest_firewall.quote: isolated containers with separate resource pools
guest_firewall.note: Browser-as-a-service in containers. Customers get only CDP and HTTP APIs, with no shell/root in the environment, so they cannot run nftables.

isolation.quote: Massively Concurrent Manage over 1,000 simultaneous browser sessions using isolated containers with separate resource pools.

image_oci.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — customers get a managed remote Chrome (CDP/HTTP API), not a machine booted from a custom Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shell/root access is exposed to run Docker inside the container.

nested_virt.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no /dev/kvm or general-purpose OS access is exposed.

desktop.quote: Live Browser Monitoring Real-time browser session monitoring with Live View and session recording
desktop.note: not offered: Live View streams the managed Chrome tab (CDP-based), not a general graphical desktop (VNC/RDP) of a full OS.

computer_use.quote: Connect seamlessly using industry-standard libraries like Puppeteer and Playwright to build powerful web automations without the complexity of managing browser infrastructure.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — automation is via CDP/Puppeteer/Playwright or JS scenarios, not a screenshot+click desktop-driving API.

ssh.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shell/SSH access to the underlying container is exposed, only a browser CDP/WS/HTTP endpoint.

snapshot.quote: Contexts enable the persistence of user data across multiple browser sessions, facilitating smoother automation, easier authentication, and improved performance optimization.
snapshot.note: No VM/filesystem or memory snapshot & restore feature is documented; 'context'/'cache' only persist the browser profile directory (cookies/cache) keyed by an id, not a point-in-time snapshot.

snapshot_auto.quote: Typically, each Browsercloud session begins with a new user data directory, meaning cookies, cache, and session storage are cleared between sessions.
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: no automatic state snapshot/restore across stop/start; state is only kept if you explicitly reuse a context/cache id.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Contexts enable the persistence of user data across multiple browser sessions
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: no API/CLI call to take a point-in-time snapshot/checkpoint of a running session.

fork.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no documented ability to clone a running browser session into new ones.

fork_running.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — depends on fork, which is not documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no fork/snapshot capability of any kind is documented.

pause_resume.quote: timeout - Session timeout (milliseconds). The limit on how long a browser instance can run.
pause_resume.note: not offered: sessions run until closed or timed out; no API to pause a running session and resume it later with reduced/paused billing.

wake_on_request.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sessions are ephemeral (spun up per connection), there is no stopped/sleeping machine that wakes on a request.

persistent_disk.quote: Browser cookies are stored within the user data directory... with Contexts, you can reuse stored data across sessions, making automation workflows faster, more reliable, and more efficient.
persistent_disk.note: Files in the browser profile (cookies/session storage) survive across sessions when a 'context' id is reused; the 'cache' param separately persists only cache data.

volume_attach.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no attachable extra storage volumes; only a browser-profile 'context'/'cache' id is documented.

volume_shared.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shared-volume concept exists for isolated browser containers.

auto_stop_idle.quote: By default session timeout is 30 seconds. You can set your value (in milliseconds) if it is needed for your script
auto_stop_idle.note: The documented behaviour is a fixed max-duration session timeout (default 30s, caller-adjustable), not idle-activity detection that stops a machine while it sits unused.

live_resize.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser instance CPU/RAM sizing is not exposed as a user-controllable, live-resizable setting.

agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — AI framework integrations (Browser Use, n8n, Zapier, Make) point the customer's own agent/framework at a CDP URL; no coding-agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) is preinstalled or offered as a template.

own_agent_api.note: Pricing page's 'Browser Agent' label is only the credit-category name for browser-hours; there is no first-party API that runs BrowserCloud's own browser/research agent. AI integrations run the agent (e.g. Browser Use) on the customer's side and point it at the CDP URL.

mcp_server.quote: Automation Frameworks Connect and automate browsers in the cloud Puppeteer Playwright Browser Use (AI browser agent) Other frameworks AI Integrations & Automation Tools Use browsers with AI platforms Browser Use n8n Make.com Zapier
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is listed among the documented integrations (Puppeteer, Playwright, Browser Use, n8n, Make.com, Zapier, HTTP API).

lang_python.note: Python examples given throughout docs (requests HTTP calls, Playwright/Pyppeteer connect_over_cdp).

lang_node.quote: import puppeteer from 'puppeteer'; const browser = await puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: `wss://chrome-v2.browsercloud.io?token=MY-TOKEN`, });
lang_node.note: JavaScript/Node.js is the primary documented client (Puppeteer, Playwright, axios HTTP examples).

public_ipv4.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no customer machine with arbitrary ports to expose; the only endpoint is the provider's fixed chrome-v2.browsercloud.io CDP/HTTP host.

inbound_https.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no feature to expose an inbound HTTPS URL to a port on a customer-run process; the browser is reached only via the provider's own endpoint.

ingress_rules.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is nothing inbound to the browser container to place access rules on beyond the API token.

egress_allowlist.quote: Proxy behavior is set by parameters proxy and proxyCountry
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: the documented network controls are customer-selected outbound proxies/geo-targeting for scraping, not a provider-side allow/deny egress list or no-internet mode.

egress_http_rules.quote: Proxy behavior is set by parameters proxy and proxyCountry
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no documented method/path-level egress rules; the closest control (blockRes) blocks resource *types* for the target page, not egress destinations.

secret_proxy.quote: Use proxyURL parameter instead of proxy & proxyCountry ProxyURL Format: socks5://proxy_login:proxy_password@domain.com:port
secret_proxy.note: Bring-your-own-proxy credentials are passed as plaintext login:password in the connection URL; there is no first-party proxy that injects credentials into arbitrary HTTP API calls so a secret never enters the machine.

static_egress_ip.note: Enterprise/Unlimited plans offer 'Custom IP Pools' (per card evidence: 'custom IP pools Enterprise/Unlimited only'); default behaviour otherwise is rotating proxy IPs, with proxySticky only holding one IP for the length of a session.

gpu.quote: Massively Concurrent Manage over 1,000 simultaneous browser sessions using isolated containers with separate resource pools.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a headless/managed-Chrome BaaS product has no GPU machine offering.

windows.quote: By default, Browsecloud uses fingerprints of real Windows OS for desktop devices. You can set another os listed below: windows, macos, linux, android, ios
windows.note: not offered: 'os' only spoofs the browser's reported OS fingerprint for anti-bot purposes; the underlying container host is Linux, not a real Windows machine.

macos.quote: By default, Browsecloud uses fingerprints of real Windows OS for desktop devices. You can set another os listed below: windows, macos, linux, android, ios
macos.note: not offered: 'os' only spoofs the browser's reported OS fingerprint; no real macOS machine is provisioned.

arm64.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CPU architecture choice is exposed to customers of this managed browser service.

self_host.quote: BrowserCloud provides enterprise-grade browser automation infrastructure through our Browsers as a Service (BaaS) platform.
self_host.note: not offered: it is a hosted SaaS (Browsers as a Service); no on-prem/self-hosted deployment package is documented.

byoc.quote: Global Infrastructure Multi-region redundancy and deployment
byoc.note: not offered: infrastructure is run by BrowserCloud on its own multi-region setup (per privacy policy, on DigitalOcean); no option to deploy the managed service into a customer's own cloud account is documented.

open_source.quote: Self-Funded Independent and accountable to customers
open_source.note: not offered: BrowserCloud is a proprietary, self-funded commercial SaaS; no OSI-licensed core product is published.

hipaa.quote: Security ISO 27001 • SOC 2 Type II compliant
hipaa.note: Only ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II are advertised; no HIPAA eligibility or BAA is mentioned anywhere on the site.

sso.quote: Enterprise For organizations with high-volume web data extraction needs, offering maximum flexibility and customization... Advanced Security Controls
sso.note: Even the Enterprise tier's feature list ('Custom RPM Limits', 'Custom Concurrency Limits', 'Bulk Discounts', 'Advanced Security Controls') does not mention SAML/OIDC single sign-on.

eu_data_residency.quote: Our residential proxy pool includes over 100 million IPs from 195 countries from over dozens of ISPs
eu_data_residency.note: Country/region controls documented are proxy geo-targeting for the target website's traffic, not a guarantee that the customer's own browser instance/data is kept in an EU region; no data-residency commitment is published.

max_session_h.quote: By default session timeout is 30 seconds. You can set your value (in milliseconds) if it is needed for your script
max_session_h.note: Only the Free plan publishes a hard cap ('Up to 15 minutes per session', per pricing page). Paid plans set their own timeout via the caller-supplied 'timeout' parameter with no published upper bound, so no fixed maximum session length is documented for the paid product.

cpu_class.quote: Lightning Fast Browser instances spin up in under 300ms. Dedicated CPUs per browser with globally distributed locations to minimize latency
cpu_class.note: The home page states browser instances get 'Dedicated CPUs per browser', which applies across all credit-pool plans (Hobby/Startup/Business share the same underlying browser-instance infrastructure). The Unlimited/dedicated-cluster mode is explicitly named a 'dedicated cluster' and inherits at least the same per-browser dedicated-CPU guarantee.

usage_api.quote: The product offers CDP and HTTP API endpoints for browser control (data scraping, PDF, screenshot, scenarios). Documentation lists no billing, usage, or account API endpoints to query per-session or per-tag usage.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; BrowserCloud is a Browsers-as-a-Service platform. Usage is tracked by credits consumed (1 browser-hour = 1,000 credits). Billing and usage data are visible only via the account dashboard; no public API exists to programmatically retrieve usage per browser session, by tag/label, or by project. The billing model charges credits at the account level against the user's monthly subscription.
